title: Central-office cost per pupil against like districts
question: Does San Francisco spend more per pupil on its central office than like districts, and did that change?
finding: The two central-office categories together cost $866 per pupil in fiscal 2019 (peer middle $644; rank 2 of 11) and $1,679 in fiscal 2024 (peer middle $1,128; rank 2 of 11), $82.6 million in all. They peaked at $1,937 per pupil in 2022-23, which was also the year of the payroll-system repair; the survey does not say what the money bought. Business and central services alone: $584 to $1,278 per pupil (peer middle $488 to $864).
how: The federal survey's "general administration" line and its "business, central and other support services" line, each divided by the district's own pupil count, for San Francisco (district and county office together) and the ten peers, fiscal 2019 to 2024. Rank 1 is the highest of the eleven.
limits: The survey does not say what is inside these lines; consultants, software, legal costs and settlements can all land here, and districts differ in what they code as central. A district that is also its own county office carries duties that peers' county offices perform for them. A district where living costs are high must pay more to hire and keep staff, and one with many small schools, or with many pupils who are learning English, have disabilities or are poor, will spend more per pupil for honest reasons; none of those is measured here.

columns.t: Business, central and other per pupil

sources.t: U.S. Census Bureau: Annual Survey of School System Finances, individual unit files, fiscal years 2015 to 2024
